title: MCP post with per_op on writes one combined program whose setup change has no stop or home: S2's operations run straight after S1's

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:mcp

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
## What happens

With the post option `per_op` ("Write one standalone program file per operation") on, the MCP `post` tool writes **one combined program**, and the setup change inside it has no stop and no home move. Setup S2's first operation follows S1's last operation directly:

```
G00 X33. Y17. Z35.
M9
M5
(SETUP: S2)
(OPERATION: F3 - FACE - G54)
G90 G54 G40 G49 G80
(T02 EM-1000-4FL - FLAT END MILL D10)
T02 M6
```

On a machine, S2's toolpath then runs on the part still mounted for S1.

## Reproduction (main 4b7a6b1e, `camcraft-cli mcp`)

```json
[["load_machine", {"builtin": "VMC 3-axis"}],
 ["add_setup", {"name": "S1"}],
 ["set_stock", {"box": {"dx": 60, "dy": 40, "dz": 10}}],
 ["add_tool", {"catalog": "EM-1000-4FL"}], ["add_tool", {"catalog": "EM-0600-4FL"}],
 ["add_operation", {"kind": "face", "tool": "EM-1000-4FL", "name": "F1"}],
 ["add_operation", {"kind": "face", "tool": "EM-0600-4FL", "name": "F2"}],
 ["add_setup", {"name": "S2", "datum_from": "S1"}],
 ["activate_setup", {"name": "S2"}],
 ["add_operation", {"kind": "face", "tool": "EM-1000-4FL", "name": "F3"}],
 ["generate", {}], ["verify", {}],
 ["set_post_options", {"per_op": true}],
 ["post", {"output": "perop.nc", "post": "Fanuc"}]]
```

`verify` is clean. `post` returns one file, `perop.nc`, 115 lines, with the excerpt above at the S1 → S2 change.

## Neighbour cases

Same document, same `post` call, only the option differs:

| Option | Output at the S1 → S2 change |
|---|---|
| default (`between_setups: "pause"`) | 119 lines: `G91 G28 Z0` / `G90` / `(SETUP CHANGE - NEXT: S2)` / `M0` |
| `between_setups: "optional-stop"` | the same with `M1` |
| `between_setups: "file-per-setup"` | two files, `..._01_S1.nc` (80 lines) and `..._02_S2.nc` (42 lines) |
| `between_setups: "continue"` | no stop: the user's explicit choice |
| `per_op: true` | no stop, and one combined file |

In the GUI, Output "One file per operation" writes "each operation as its own standalone program into a folder" (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/pages.rs`, #111). The browser build refuses that post outright (`browser_files::refusal`, `NO_FOLDER`). Neither GUI path writes this combined program.

## Root cause (confirmed)

- `stop_of` in `crates/app/src/posting_setup_change.rs` returns no stop whenever `per_op` is set ("run straight on, one file per setup, or one file per operation"). The stop is dropped in the stream, before any post script runs, so every post is affected.
- The MCP `post` tool calls the script API's `v_post` (`crates/app/src/script/api.rs`). That writes through `posting::post_mounts_script_with_options` / `post_mounts_with_script_options`: one program per mount, and never `post_per_op`.

So `per_op` removes the stop that only per-operation files make safe, and this path then writes the operations into one file anyway. The same holds for a script's `cam.post`.

## Expected

The MCP `post` (and `cam.post`) with `per_op` on writes one file per operation, as the GUI does, or refuses by name. It must never write a combined program whose setup change has lost its stop.

## Suggested labels

Outside contributors can't set labels, so these are suggestions:

- `P1`: wrong posted G-code; a setup change runs on without the operator's stop.
